prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1348; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a rear-end collision on a major roadway in Sugar Land, Texas. Driver 1 was stopped in traffic when the rear of their vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was traveling at a speed too high for the conditions. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash, and the force of the impact appeared sufficient to produce that kind of injury. Driver 2 acknowledged following too closely and stated that the collision happened the way Driver 1 described. Two independent witnesses gave statements that matched this account. Officers photographed the scene and both vehicles. The damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle and the front of Driver 2's vehicle lined up with the direction and severity of the impact, and officers found no prior damage to either vehicle at the scene. A Passenger was also in Driver 1's vehicle, and both the witnesses and the responding officers confirmed that person's presence at the time of the crash. Driver 1 was identified as the named insured on the policy for the vehicle involved.
